summary: The note describes the People's Vanguard Party, a Ba'athist political party in South Yemen that was aligned with the Syrian-based Ba'ath Party. It covers the party's general secretary, Abdallah Badhib, who was appointed Minister of Education in December 1969. It also explains that the party was one of two non-National Front parties tolerated in the early 1970s and that it joined the NF-dominated United Political Organization in October 1975, a merger ratified at the third PVP congress in August 1975.
one_line: The People's Vanguard Party was a Ba'athist party in South Yemen that merged into the NF-dominated United Political Organization in 1975.
key_facts: The People's Vanguard Party was a Ba'athist political party in South Yemen.
The People's Vanguard Party was aligned with the Syrian-based Ba'ath Party.
Abdallah Badhib was the general secretary of the People's Vanguard Party.
Abdallah Badhib was appointed Minister of Education in December 1969.
The People's Vanguard Party was one of two non-National Front parties tolerated during the early 1970s.
In October 1975 the People's Vanguard Party joined the NF-dominated United Political Organization.
The United Political Organization evolved into the Yemeni Socialist Party in 1978.
The merger of the People's Vanguard Party into the United Political Organization was ratified by the third PVP congress held in August 1975.
